newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc boosted by Rorer results.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc boosted by Rorer results.

text.p: Shares in chemical company Rhone-Poulenc rose by over four percent to 183.50 francs at 0937 GMT on the back of a 25 percent increase in 1996 profits at its pharmaceutical unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
"The figures are at the top end of expectations," a dealer said.
Rorer said on Monday its 1996 net attributable income rose by 25 percent to $428.7 million while its earnings per share were up at $3.16.
The company said that the earnings would have been higher but for the costs of an albumin product recall at the Centeon LCC joint venture with Hoechst of Germany.

Centeon restarted its production on January 24 after an October 10 product recall for a potential risk of bacterial infection. Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said the 1996 costs of the recall were $0.44 per share.
A company official said he expected synergies from the 1995 acquisition of Fisons to exceed $200 million in 1997.
A company spokeswoman said that in 1996 the synergies were neutral.
